analysis.title: What's Trending Across Credit (Alisha Pasi, FICC & Equities, 25 Oct 2026)
key_insights: The AI trade's debate has shifted from how much capital is deployed to how much financing the market can absorb, who bears the risk, and whether the economics justify the investment.

Pressure moved up the capital structure last week from neoclouds to hyperscalers: strong operating results were overshadowed by large capex plans and a crowded financing pipeline. GS's 30Y hyperscaler basket widened +17bps on the week and is 85bps cheap to IG100 ex-hyperscalers.
HY AI-related spreads widened +78bps over two weeks, versus +22bps for non-AI HY excluding CCCs.

The backdrop includes oil above $100, escalating Middle East tensions, European sovereign stress and volatile rates. The market is not indiscriminate risk-off: generic IG is resilient, BB credit draws demand and well-structured new issues clear.

IG spreads widened about +5bps on the week, but the weakness is concentrated in hyperscalers, crowded TMT exposures and select European financials. Money centers, non-AI industrials and energy held in better. TMT weakness reflects absence of natural buyers more than outright selling.

IG primary: $24.6bn priced across 14 deals, nearly 65% of issuance inside seven years. Walmart and Kimberly-Clark benefited from demand for diversification away from AI supply. Average tightening from IPTs was 26.6bps, books 3.1x covered, average new-issue concession 4.1bps.

October IG supply is near $71bn against a $130bn Street estimate. Possible additional hyperscaler financing arrives as European credit faces political and sovereign pressure, limiting an alternative outlet for USD supply.

HY spreads widened about 6bps, but the index masks three markets: resilient generic credit, an AI universe being repriced, and lower-quality issuers under severe stress. About 40% of HY bonds still trade inside +200bps. AI-related HY spreads are near +400bps. CCC spreads reached about +1,127bps, a four-year wide.

CCC stress is concentrated in single names: nearly 90% of CCC bonds by notional declined over 60 days, daily price moves run 3.3x those of BBs, and the 20 worst bonds fell an average of 14.3pts in October, nearly half the bucket's total point losses. 59% of the HY market reports earnings by end of November.

JetBlue loyalty bonds fell more than 30pts over nine sessions to the low $40s and recovered to about $44.5 by Friday, on sentiment, systematic selling and thin liquidity rather than one catalyst. Rising jet fuel is a broader airline problem: Alaska and WestJet loans fell about 4.5pts and 9pts on the week.

CDX IG and HY ended the week near recent wides on AI credit stress, oil and European politics. HY, CCCs and AI-exposed single names absorbed more pressure than generic IG synthetics. Flows were two-way, with short covering repeatedly giving way to renewed hedging.

Crude rose above $100/bbl on Strait of Hormuz tensions. Treasuries rallied on safe-haven demand and the 10Y briefly traded through 5%, before stronger flash PMI selling-price data challenged the move. Ahead of the FOMC the market is caught between growth concerns and inflation pressure.

French political unrest and sovereign spread widening weighed on European financials and credit sentiment, with possible spillover into cross-currency funding and a less accommodating European issuance window for USD supply.

Positioning: equity hedge funds are cutting gross exposure aggressively while systematic rates strategies remain heavily short duration. GS estimates bond CTAs are short about $145mm DV01 globally, so further yield declines could force short covering.

GS Prime: hedge funds had their largest weekly de-grossing since July and systematic long/short had its worst week since 2024. The GS Momentum basket has had 30 daily moves of 5% or more this year, more than any prior year in the dataset. BG leans toward later innings of a positioning unwind rather than the start of a prolonged AI repricing.

Equities desk (Coppersmith): Thursday was the first simultaneous 1%+ drawdown across fundamental L/S, systematic and multi-strategy funds since COVID. HF gross leverage is 312% (96th percentile). Modeled CTA S&P selling is $11.6bn in a flat week and up to $65bn in a larger one-month selloff. The desk sees possible relief rally if earnings stabilize sentiment and favors defined-risk upside.

GS Mortgage desk sees value in non-QM AAA RMBS at +155-160bps over Treasuries, about 30bps wider since July, 2-3yr base-case WAL. In agency MBS it prefers FN 5.0s-5.5s strategically, with tactical opportunities in FN 2.0s-2.5s.

Upcoming catalysts: FOMC (GS preview titled 'Hiking at a Slower Pace'), mega-cap tech earnings, potential Meta and SpaceX financing supply, and the midterms. GS M&A credit trader says M&A is on track for a record with focus on financing mix.

tension_points.bull_case: BG leans toward later innings of a positioning unwind rather than the start of prolonged AI repricing, and the equities desk sees a possible relief rally if earnings stabilize sentiment.
tension_points.bear_case: Hyperscaler financing needs may outpace investor appetite, with a crowded pipeline, limited natural buyers and hedge fund de-grossing compounding the repricing.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A poorly received next hyperscaler financing (potential Meta or SpaceX supply) or disappointing mega-cap tech earnings.

tension_points.bull_case: Growth concerns and safe-haven demand pull yields lower, and CTA short covering could extend a rally.
tension_points.bear_case: Oil above $100 and strong flash PMI selling prices renew inflation pressure and limit Fed flexibility.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The 10Y moving back through 5% after strong inflation data.
